definition: The year immediately following the Financial Year in which your income is assessed and taxed. For FY 2025-26, the AY is 2026-27.
Tax paid in installments throughout the year (instead of a lump sum at the end) if your total tax liability is ₹10,000 or more.
A tax on tax. The Health and Education Cess is currently 4% of your income tax plus surcharge.
An amount subtracted from your gross income to reduce your taxable income (e.g., under Section 80C).
A specific type of income that is completely excluded from tax calculation (e.g., HRA exemption, agricultural income).
The year in which you earn your income, running from April 1 to March 31. Currently FY 2026-27.
A certificate issued by your employer detailing your salary and the TDS deducted during the year.
A consolidated tax statement showing all TDS deducted, taxes paid, and refunds issued against your PAN.
The sum of all your income (salary, house property, business, capital gains, other sources) before claiming deductions.
A salary component paid to cover rented accommodation. It is partially or fully exempt from tax under Section 10(13A).
Adjusting the purchase price of an asset for inflation to reduce your capital gains tax. (Largely removed for property in FY 2023-24 onwards).
The form you submit to the government declaring your income, deductions, and tax paid for the year.
Profit from selling an asset (like property or stocks) held for more than a specified period (e.g., 12 months for stocks, 24 months for property).
A government-backed retirement savings scheme. Contributions qualify for additional tax deductions under Section 80CCD(1B).
A unique 10-character alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department.
A tax credit available to resident individuals with income below a certain threshold (e.g., ₹12,00,000 in the new regime for FY 2026-27).
Profit from selling an asset held for a short period (e.g., less than 12 months for stocks). Usually taxed at a higher rate than LTCG.
An additional tax levied on high-income earners (e.g., 10% on income above ₹50 Lakhs) on top of the base income tax.
Tax withheld by the payer (like an employer or bank) and deposited directly with the government on your behalf.
Tax collected by a seller (e.g., on foreign remittances or car purchases) and deposited with the government.
Your Gross Total Income minus all eligible deductions. This is the amount on which your tax rate is actually applied.
The legal term for cryptocurrency and NFTs. Taxed under Section 115BBH at a flat 30% without deductions.
